title: HB3268 (2021 Regular): Relating to weapons in the Capitol.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Oregon) (gun-policy Stage 5, Oregon); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Oregon text (Introduced, official copy, https://olis.oregonlegislature.gov/liz/2021R1/Downloads/MeasureDocument/HB3268/Introduced; sha256 f310272c2512788bb67a2c4f688bcb89c33570fc85493cc92b06178f2eb691b2)
provenance.note: Version read: introduced (as filed). Sections 2 and 3 (ORS 166.380, 166.262) change how concealed-license holders are treated in the Capitol (no license shortcut for examination or arrest). Subsection (1)(b) text may include old words; the summary says the Capitol ban is the bill's change. No passage vote recorded.

operative_text:
SECTION 1 (ORS 166.370): (b) Any person who intentionally possesses a loaded or unloaded firearm, or any other instrument used as a dangerous weapon, while in the Capitol shall upon conviction be guilty of a Class C felony.
SECTION 1 (ORS 166.370): (5) Subsection (1)(b) of this section does not apply to: (a) A police officer as that term is defined in ORS 181A.355. (b) An active or reserve member of the military forces of this state or the United States, when engaged in the performance of duty.
SECTION 4 (ORS 173.720): (3) The Legislative Administrator shall develop and implement an administrative policy for the screening of persons entering the State Capitol by security personnel before admission into the building.
